children: Rocket Lab (RKLB) shares climbed 2% on early Wednesday as investors weighed progress on the company's Neutron rocket alongside continued uncertainty over its first flight.

Rocket Lab expects to move the first Neutron vehicle to its launch pad during the fourth quarter. However, the company has not provided a specific launch date, leaving the timing of the debut dependent on qualification work and testing.

The delay matters because Neutron is central to the company's longer-term growth case. A pressure-test failure involving the rocket's first-stage tank earlier this year pushed the expected debut from mid-2026 toward the end of the year, with another slip into 2027 possible.

Rocket Lab's existing operations continue to expand. Second-quarter revenue reached a record $234 million, up 62% from a year earlier, while management expects third-quarter revenue of $250 million to $265 million.

The company ended June with about $2.4 billion in cash and marketable securities after raising roughly $1.5 billion through stock sales during the first half. That liquidity could provide additional time to complete Neutron development, although further delays may extend the wait for meaningful profitability.

title: Rocket Lab Stock Climbs. Yet Neutron Launch Date Remains Out of Reach
